introduction.definition: Wear rings are renewable rings — one on the impeller eye, one in the casing — forming a small running clearance between the high-pressure discharge side and the low-pressure eye. They limit internal recirculation and are the sacrificial parts that wear instead of the impeller and casing.

pressure.title: Clearance separates high and low pressure
pressure.description: The impeller discharge pressure acts in the gap between the front shroud and the casing; only the narrow wear-ring clearance separates it from the low-pressure eye. Leakage through the clearance is recirculated inside the pump, wasting energy: as rings wear and clearance doubles, efficiency can fall several points. Typical diametral clearance ≈ 0.25–0.5 mm for 50–150 mm rings (API 610 sets minimums by diameter and material). Replace rings when clearance reaches about twice the new value.

wear.description: Wear rings are the sacrificial surfaces: dissimilar, galling-resistant materials and hardness differences are used.

video_tutorials.title: Wear Ring — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Wear Ring.
Wear rings are renewable rings — one on the impeller eye, one in the casing — forming a small running clearance between the high-pressure discharge side and the low-pressure eye.
They limit internal recirculation and are the sacrificial parts that wear instead of the impeller and casing.
Typical applications include closed-impeller centrifugal pumps; multistage pumps (also interstage bushings).
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Closed Impeller (turning), Suction Cover & Casing (section).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Wear Ring.
Trend pump performance (flow/head/power).
Measure clearance at overhaul.
Replace rings when ≈ 2× new clearance.
Watch for excess clearance: lower head and efficiency. Common cause: abrasive wear, erosion.
Watch for galling / seizure: pump locks, damage. Common cause: same materials, tight clearance, dry run.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
